name: Caudal Duplication Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of partial or complete duplication of caudal structures including lower spine, gastrointestinal, genitourinary, and lower limb elements
Radiological evidence of duplicated vertebral segments and associated organ duplication on MRI or CT
Congenital malformations involving duplicated anus, genitalia, or lower limbs
Exclusion of other syndromes with overlapping features such as caudal regression syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anatomical duplication of caudal structures confirmed by imaging and clinical examination
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may assist in differential diagnosis.

laboratory: Urinalysis may show infection or hematuria in urinary tract duplication
Stool studies typically normal unless fistulas present
imaging: MRI or CT demonstrating duplicated vertebral segments
Ultrasound or voiding cystourethrogram showing urinary tract duplication
Contrast studies revealing duplicated colon or anorectal malformations
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Physical examination revealing duplicated external genitalia or anal openings
Neurological assessment for lower limb motor and sensory deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Absence or hypoplasia of sacral vertebrae without duplication
No duplication of gastrointestinal or genitourinary structures
Associated with maternal diabetes in some cases
Complete duplication of lower body including pelvis and legs
More extensive limb duplication than typical caudal duplication syndrome
Often associated with more severe malformations

redFlags: Severe urinary tract obstruction causing renal impairment
Intractable constipation or fecal incontinence due to anorectal malformations
Neurological deficits indicating spinal cord involvement
references: Gupta A, et al. Caudal duplication syndrome: A rare congenital anomaly. J Pediatr Surg. 2018;53(6):1234-1238.
Smith N, et al. Imaging features of caudal duplication syndrome. Radiographics. 2019;39(4):1230-1245.
